specs.scene: A documentary photograph of a young adult sitting cross-legged on a worn couch, a laptop balanced on their knees, hands mid-type, the screen tilted away and blank, soft daylight falling through a window behind them, a plain domestic living room with nothing else in frame, no other people, no visible logos or readable text.
specs.source_quote: The barrier that used to stop you from shipping software is just gone.

recognisable.why: a person with a laptop on a couch is an everyday scene but not a named brand or distinctive trade, so recognition is moderate rather than instant.

legibility.why: person and laptop resolve as one focal mass at small size.

curiosity.why: the flat verdict names no barrier and no mechanism, leaving the viewer wanting the specifics.

subject.why: a person mid-action is a clear single anchor.

credible.why: no figure is carried, which the rubric scores full.

stakes.why: a removed barrier to shipping software implies direct personal opportunity or threat to the viewer's own plans.

reexpress.why: the overlay closely mirrors the title's own claim that you no longer need to code, restating rather than splitting the work.
